Long ago, a hungry dragon woke up. Fearsome Zhaitan emerged from a long sleep, intent on eating the whole world. His awakening caused a massive wave, which tore across the ocean—straight for Cantha.

The people looked on in terror as it came their way. No one knew what to do. No one, that is, except for the saltspray dragon Kuunavang. She told the emperor and empress, "I will get help. Keep the people safe." And so noble Kuunavang flew as fast as she could to the home of the great dragon Soo-Won.

"Soo-Won!" she cried. "We need you! A great wave is coming, and it will wash away the people of Cantha!" Hearing her words, Soo-Won rose from the Endless Ocean and said, "I will come," and together, the two dragons flew to where the raging water now washed over Cantha.

When they arrived, the flood had already destroyed the city of Kaineng, and the people were running, fast as they could, deeper into Cantha, the wave chasing right at their heels. With a swoop of great wings, Soo-Won landed, placing herself between the wave and the people.

She stared down the oncoming water and commanded it, "Stop." The wave crashed in front of Soo-Won, as if an invisible cliff now stood in front of her. The water raged, swirling and splashing, trying to get through, but then the great dragon gave a second command, "Retreat."

The wave had no choice but to obey. It recoiled and slipped backward, slowly and gently, so that it could do no more harm as it retreated back to the ocean. The people of Cantha cheered for Soo-Won, and they cheered for noble Kuunavang.

But Soo-Won did not stay to take part in the celebrations. She slipped away, with a promise that she would always be nearby, and that if another disaster should strike, she would return. Until then, she would rest. And noble Kuunavang stayed among the humans so that if time came, she could wake Soo-Won once again. And the people of Cantha rested easy, knowing they had two dragons watching over them as they slept.

Commander,

Very exciting news! A crystalline resonance cascade scenario has occurred! You can read my upcoming publication...wait. That book already exists; it's right here on my desk.

This already happened!

Okay, so, remember when all of your green prophet shards and crystals turned blue? Maybe you don't; I somehow forgot. That was the primary crystalline resonance cascade scenario—it happened a while ago! BUT! NOW! This is so amazing: it REBOUNDS! I thought the original scenario passed and was done. All my theories are wrong! This book is blissfully foul and wrong! I don't deserve this truly massive shelf full of awards and accolades! I have to go throw it all out and consult my crystals! Red prophet shards don't even exist! Why would I write about them?

I'm back. This is fine. Everything is fine. I don't care what Phlunt says—crystallography has not been turned on its sixth axis at all. We're OK. This is just going to keep happening periodically and that's fine.

Your green prophet shards have turned blue. Again. My associate Zazzl now collects blue shards because all the shards in Cantha are blue now. This is just the world we live in.

I'm assigning another protege—very smart kid—Nikki, to go find where the locus of green shards is centering. She'll take them off your hands until the next rebound event.

%str1%, interested in a bit of fieldwork for the Durmand Priory?

As you're well aware, Tyria has experienced historical events at an incredible pace in recent years. We're undoubtedly in the midst of a changing of ages—a time that will be looked back on as a pivotal one.

It falls to us to record it all as best as we can, especially now that we've reached a well-earned time of peace. The Priory has dispatched a team to the Grove to gather accounts related to events just prior to the Pact's Maguuma campaign, a period of time that both you and I found ourselves involved in. It would be a great help if you lent a hand, both in recounting your perspective of events and securing relevant areas for our less combat-inclined members to survey.

My team and I will be conducting interviews near the entrance to the Grove. Why not drop by and regale us with a tale or two?
